subject: Mathematics
learning_objective: Students will solve quadratic equations using factoring and the quadratic formula, and interpret the discriminant.
explanation: Quadratic equations take the standard form ax² + bx + c = 0. Roots are the values of x that make the equation true, found via factoring or the quadratic formula x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / 2a.

common_misconceptions.name: Missing negative root
common_misconceptions.description: Student forgets that x² = k yields both positive and negative roots x = ±√k.
common_misconceptions.remediation: Always write x = ±√k when taking the square root of both sides of an equation.

common_misconceptions.name: Sign error in quadratic formula
common_misconceptions.description: Student misapplies -b when b is already negative.

worked_example:
Solve x² - 5x + 6 = 0.
Step 1: Factor into (x - 2)(x - 3) = 0.
Step 2: Set each factor equal to zero: x - 2 = 0 or x - 3 = 0.
Step 3: Solutions are x = 2 and x = 3.
citations: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics - High School Algebra
